audit.whatIsWrong: The page tells the player to use Defiant Dance to eat Rumble's damage in four places — the TL;DR ('W his R line'), the win condition, the early paragraph ('Defiant Dance's damage reduction lets you eat a Flamespitter tick or an Electro Harpoon poke') and wants.you[1]. Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage only. Flamespitter, Electro Harpoon, The Equalizer and the overheat auto bonus are all magic.
audit.why: Riot's W text: 'She takes reduced physical damage during the charge.' Every damage source in Rumble's kit is magic, so the reduction applies to none of it. The mirror audit on rumble__irelia reached the identical conclusion from the other side and called it the highest-value addition on that page. This is not a wording nit: the player is being told to hold a defensive button through a burst it does not touch.
audit.corrected: Defiant Dance blunts nothing here. Magic resist is the mitigation — and Electro Harpoon reduces it, so buy it earlier than feels natural.

audit.whatIsWrong: Electro Harpoon's magic resist reduction is never mentioned, despite the entry's core instruction being 'build MR'. Scrap Shield's cooldown is never given.
audit.why: Riot's E text: 'reducing their Magic Resist. Rumble can carry 2 harpoons at a time.' So the one stat the page tells you to buy is the stat he shreds, twice per rotation. And Scrap Shield is a FLAT 6s at every rank — the shortest cooldown in the matchup, which is why opening into a fresh one wastes your combo.
audit.corrected: Both stated: harpoon cuts MR and he holds two charges; Scrap Shield is 6s flat and is his shield and his only escape at once.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows disagreed with their own whys text. whys[0] and whys[1] describe Rumble bullying the lane while the rows read Irelia and Skill; whys[2] says 'it's a coinflip read' with the row reading Rumble; whys[3] and whys[5] describe Irelia winning with the rows reading Rumble; whys[6] says 'it stays even' with the row reading Rumble.
audit.why: The packet chart (Rumble, Rumble, Skill, Irelia, Irelia, Irelia, Skill) matches the prose on every single row.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 flipped in matched full/content pairs; 3/10 Rumble, 5/10 even, 7/10 Irelia.

audit.whatIsWrong: First-item spike named 'Trinity Force / bruiser core' in whys[5], spikes[3].text and late against an itemization block that builds Blade of the Ruined King; and Irelia's passive credited with 'resist shred' in whys[5], spikes[3].text, mid ('your armor-shredded target') and late.
audit.why: Ionian Fervor is stacking Attack Speed plus bonus on-hit at max stacks. The mirror audit removed the same fabrication from the Rumble-side page.
audit.corrected: Renamed throughout. The Equalizer's 130s rank-1 cooldown added as the real spike to track.

edits.before: Rumble owns the opening levels — Flamespitter is a sustained cone that out-trades you in melee while you have only Q and no stun to punish him. Don't walk into the flame stream to contest a last-hit; tag the casters with Bladesurge and accept you're farming, not trading. Defiant Dance's damage reduction lets you eat a Flamespitter tick or an Electro Harpoon poke without taking the full hit, but until you have E at 3 you can't open a real all-in. Once you do, bait or wait out his Scrap Shield move-speed, then drop Flawless Duet — his harpoon slow can't kite a dash that's already stunned him in place.
edits.after: Rumble owns the opening levels — Flamespitter is a sustained 3-second cone that out-trades you in melee while you have only Q and no stun to punish him. Don't walk into the flame stream to contest a last-hit; tag the casters with Bladesurge and accept you're farming, not trading. Do not count on Defiant Dance here: it cuts physical damage only and every point of his kit is magic, so it blunts nothing. Until you have E at 3 you can't open a real all-in. Once you do, bait his Scrap Shield — 6s flat — then drop Flawless Duet; his harpoon slow can't kite a dash that has already stunned him.

edits.before: This is where the lane tilts to you. Your Bladesurge passive stacks up and your cooldowns tighten, so once you stun him with Flawless Duet he can't just Electro Harpoon and walk — he's stuck in melee range with you. The key read is his Scrap Shield: it's his shield AND his only move-speed out, so don't open into it; hold your E until it's spent, then all-in. At 6, Vanguard's Edge walls off his retreat — he's dash-less, so the blade wall plus your Bladesurge resets means he burns before his Flamespitter and overheat autos can out-DPS your armor-shredded target.

At 6, Vanguard's Edge walls off his retreat — he's dash-less, so the blade wall plus your Bladesurge resets burn him before Flamespitter and his overheat autos out-DPS you.

edits.before: Your first item (Trinity Force or bruiser core) is your peak — full Bladesurge reset uptime, max-stack passive resist shred, and Defiant Dance's damage reduction make you the favourite in the all-in, so force the trade here before his AP scaling matters. The one thing to respect all game is The Equalizer: he'll drop the line right under you mid-trade to flip it, so bait the ult or reposition out of it with a Bladesurge reset rather than fighting on top of fresh fire. Close on your mid-game lead — at full items his poke-and-zone Danger Zone pattern can stall you out if you let him scale even.
edits.after: Your first item (Blade of the Ruined King) is your peak — full Bladesurge reset uptime and max Ionian Fervor attack speed make you the favourite in the all-in, so force the trade here before his AP scaling matters. Don't plan around Defiant Dance blunting anything: it reduces physical only and his kit is entirely magic, so magic resist is the real mitigation — and Electro Harpoon cuts into it.
